strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly identifies genuine limitations of pixel-aligned Gaussian models (computational costs quadratic in views/resolution, excessive redundant Gaussians) with concrete examples (200M vs 0.5M Gaussians).

Sensible architectural design: Decoupling scene representation from images and two-stage attention (per-view cross-attention + global self-attention) are intuitive solutions that meaningfully reduce complexity.

Comprehensive experimental validation: Evaluation across multiple datasets (RE10K, DL3DV, ACID) with varied configurations (2-8+ views, multiple resolutions), cross-dataset generalization, and wide-coverage settings.
Thorough ablation studies: Table 7 (depth), Table 8 (components), and supplementary ablations systematically validate design choices, though some remain superficial.
Strong and consistent quantitative results: Superior performance on DL3DV (27.90 vs 24.28 PSNR vs DepthSplat) and wide-coverage settings (0.53s vs 0.61s vs LongLRM).
Reproducibility: Extensive implementation details, hyperparameters, training protocols, and code configuration provided for reproducibility.
weaknesses: Misleading iterative refinement framing: The core claim of iterative refinement mimicking optimization-based methods is problematic. Each layer processes frozen input images with no actual error-feedback loop unlike true optimization methods (render → measure error → update). This is progressive refinement through depth, not iterative optimization. No visualizations show how representations evolve across layers.

Unfair experimental comparisons: Primary results tables emphasize 8-view configuration while baselines use 2-4 views. While Table 1 shows fairer 2,F,F comparison, most results conflate architectural improvements with using more views. Different training setups (GPU type, batch size, iterations) across experiments complicate attribution. GS-LRM marked unavailable with single PSNR reported.

Insufficient analysis of iterative refinement benefits: Ablation in Table 8 ('w/o iter. refinement') compares architecturally different configurations (1 cross + 11 self vs 12 alternating), not a clean ablation. No layer-wise analysis showing which layers refine coarse vs fine details. Missing comparison with depth-matched single-pass alternatives that would isolate iterative benefits.

Limited technical novelty: Primarily combines existing techniques (cross-attention, self-attention, token expansion) in a straightforward way. Cross+self-attention is standard in vision transformers. Token uplifting is conventional query expansion. Decoupling representations is intuitive but incremental compared to prior embedding-based approaches (LRM, Lara).

Scalability claims not fully supported: Method still uses self-attention across viewpoint embeddings (O(V²)). While better than full cross-view attention, this contradicts scalability claims. Section 4 acknowledges this bottleneck. Marginal PSNR gains from 6→24 views (25.60→27.38) suggest diminishing returns; 32-view setting doesn't demonstrate breakthrough scalability.

Design choices lack justification: Token uplifting factor k=2 is 'empirically set' without ablation. Mini-batch cross-attention variants (Fig. 4) show clear degradation (30.39→30.08 PSNR, Table 6) with insufficient analysis. Patch size p=8 not ablated. Table 7 shows monotonic improvement with depth, yet 12 layers chosen without justification. Plücker ray encoding choice not validated.

Compactness claims insufficiently supported: Gaussian counts vary widely (172K-688K, Table 3) without clear pattern. Missing iso-quality comparison (for same PSNR, how many Gaussians?) to rigorously demonstrate claimed compactness advantage over pixel-aligned methods.

Absent failure analysis and robustness evaluation: No discussion of failure cases or challenging scenarios (reflections, transparent materials, thin structures). All qualitative results appear reasonable—are there failure modes? No robustness analysis to camera pose noise despite requiring known poses. No evaluation on in-the-wild unposed data.

Statistical rigor: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Improvements often modest (0.2-1.0 PSNR). No evaluation of variance across multiple runs or initialization sensitivity, limiting confidence in claimed improvements.

Incomplete technical details: How sensitive is performance to viewpoint embedding initialization? How does it scale with scene complexity (object count, geometric intricacy)? Gradient flow through rendering not analyzed. Why Plücker rays specifically? Limited evaluation of metric sensitivity (only PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS; no perceptual or user studies).

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification with concrete examples (200M redundant Gaussians) and clear articulation of scalability limitations in existing methods
Elegant architectural design combining decoupling strategy, two-stage attention scheme, and token uplifting to effectively reduce computational complexity while maintaining reconstruction quality
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple large-scale datasets (RE10K, DL3DV, ACID) with consistent improvements in quality and significant efficiency gains (~4× speedup vs DepthSplat)
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 7-9) validating design choices and demonstrating importance of iterative refinement, resolution decoupling, and token uplifting mechanisms
Strong scalability demonstration showing graceful handling of 8+ viewpoints with computation under half of baseline methods
Practical efficiency benefits: more compact Gaussian representations (e.g., 65K vs 131K Gaussians) without quality sacrifice, faster inference (0.025s), and reduced memory footprint
Excellent presentation with clear figures (particularly Fig. 2 showing computational reduction), detailed implementation details, and comprehensive supplementary material supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: contributions are primarily architectural combination of existing components (iterative refinement, Plücker embeddings, attention mechanisms, token expansion) rather than fundamental innovations

Self-attention bottleneck acknowledged but unresolved: claimed scalability limited to ~8-32 views; self-attention remains O(N²) in number of views with no proposed alternative, weakening scalability claims

Experimental comparisons lack fairness: Table 5 compares 0.5s inference to 13min optimization on different hardware (H100 vs A100), making 'outperforms optimization methods' claim in abstract misleading; training setups vary across experiments

Iterative refinement mechanism underexplored: analogy to optimization is loose (cross-attention guidance ≠ gradient-based updates); lacks visualization of layer-wise improvements and clear analysis of what drives performance gains
Requires known camera poses from COLMAP/SfM, limiting applicability to raw video and unstructured data; pose-free setting mentioned only as future work despite growing relevance

Modest quantitative improvements in several cases: many gains from using more viewpoints (8 vs 2) rather than algorithmic improvements; PSNR gains often <1.5 dB vs baselines with different training setup
Limited ablation on key hyperparameters: token uplifting factor k=2 set empirically with insufficient sensitivity analysis; patch size p=8 and layer count selection not thoroughly justified
DL3DV experiments use finetuning from RE10K-trained model rather than training from scratch, complicating isolated evaluation and making generalization claims less clear

Missing analysis: no failure cases, limited discussion of when 3D-GS representation becomes limiting, spherical harmonics omission not justified, and no visualization of iterative refinement progression

strengths: Well-motivated approach addressing practical scalability challenges in feed-forward 3D reconstruction with clear problem formulation
Comprehensive experimental validation across large-scale datasets (REIO10K, DL3DV) with extensive metrics, ablations, and multiple evaluation settings demonstrating thorough empirical rigor

Effective architectural design with decoupled viewpoint-independent representation enabling practical efficiency gains (0.5s inference time, reduced memory usage) while maintaining competitive reconstruction quality
Strong empirical results showing superior performance to optimization-based approaches and comparable results to recent feed-forward methods with good scalability across varying view counts
Excellent supplementary material with detailed implementation details, additional ablations, and qualitative visualizations (depth maps, geometry, zero-shot synthesis) supporting reproducibility
Multiple efficient cross-attention variants explored with principled design for reducing computational overhead while preserving visual consistency
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty with individual components (viewpoint tokenization, cross-attention, iterative refinement) being relatively standard techniques; contribution is primarily in effective combination rather than fundamental innovation

Modest improvements over recent feed-forward baselines (DepthSplat, MVSplat) with often <0.5 PSNR gains, and performance advantages diminish under fair comparison with identical view configurations (Table 17)
Critical dependency on accurate camera poses without adequate robustness analysis; real-world applicability compromised as method cannot estimate poses independently
Incomplete scaling analysis limited to 32 views and 512×960 resolution; behavior with significantly more views or higher resolutions unexplored; memory requirements grow rapidly with view count
Fair comparison concerns due to baseline models trained with different view configurations and resolutions, making direct quantitative comparisons ambiguous and potentially misleading
Brief limitations discussion lacking systematic failure mode analysis; unclear which scene types or configurations challenge the method or when iterative refinement provides marginal benefits

Primarily empirical work lacking theoretical grounding; no formal analysis of convergence properties, information flow through refinement layers, or principled justification for architectural choices beyond empirical validation

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation with extensive ablations (Tables 6-9) systematically validating each architectural component across multiple datasets (RE10K, DL3DV, ACID)

Practical efficiency improvements demonstrated with 0.5-second inference while maintaining competitive quality, addressing a real computational bottleneck through thoughtful decoupling of HR image tokens from viewpoint representations
Solid empirical results showing improvements over recent baselines (MVSplat, DepthSplat, Long-LRM) across standard metrics in various configurations
Well-designed cross-attention and self-attention mechanisms for multi-view context modeling with structured mini-batch sampling strategies
Good qualitative visualizations and attention analysis (Figures 5-8) demonstrating the method functions as intended
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: Core components (cross-attention, self-attention, Gaussian splatting) are well-established; the main contribution is engineering-focused combination rather than fundamental innovation. The iterative refinement amounts to stacking similar blocks without clear theoretical justification for why this approach is optimal.

Experimental setup concerns compromise fair comparison: Different batch sizes across methods (12 vs. 16), inconsistent training regimes (some baselines use pre-trained checkpoints vs. iLRM trained from scratch), and varying view configurations make it difficult to isolate the method's true contribution

Critical limitations inadequately addressed: Severe reliance on accurate camera poses (acknowledged but not thoroughly investigated); supplementary pose perturbation evaluation (Table 14) is insufficient. Robustness to pose noise during inference is not analyzed, severely limiting real-world applicability

Marginal performance gains with high computational cost: Table 6 shows diminishing returns (e.g., 9→12 layers yields only 0.32 PSNR improvement for (4,H,P,F) configuration). Performance plateaus quickly, questioning whether the iterative refinement philosophy is justified

Insufficient justification for design choices: Why is the specific cross-attention architecture optimal? Token uplifting strategy (Eq. 2) appears ad-hoc without comparison to alternatives. The paper lacks theoretical explanation for what each iteration learns

Scalability claims not rigorously supported: Demonstrations limited to 32 input views at 540×960; behavior with 100+ views or very high resolutions remains unexplored. Training memory requirements only briefly mentioned; claims of 'scalability improvements' need more rigorous analysis

Presentation clarity issues: Dense notation and complex Equations 1-5; Figure 2 is difficult to parse; Figure 4 (attention schemes) lacks clear labeling. The relationship between HR/LR image tokens and viewpoint tokens needs better explanation. Section 3.2 would benefit from substantial rewriting

Standard training formulation: Equation 5 uses conventional MSE + perceptual loss. The iterative refinement concept does not inspire novel training objectives or loss formulations specific to the problem

Reproducibility concerns: No code release mentioned; training details are vague regarding augmentation strategies, learning rate schedules, and stage-specific hyperparameters. These details are essential for reproduction

strengths: Well-motivated iterative refinement architecture with three clearly articulated core principles that effectively address limitations in existing feed-forward 3D reconstruction methods
Comprehensive experimental validation across three large-scale datasets (RE10K, DL3DV, ACID) with consistent improvements over multiple strong baselines on PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 6, 8-9) systematically validating each design component's contribution to the final performance
Significant practical efficiency gains: achieves 0.5-second inference while generating 4-7x fewer Gaussians than baselines, enabling real-time applications
Demonstrates robust scalability with respect to number of input views (16-256) and resolution variations, with graceful performance degradation
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figures 2-4, 13-18) showing both qualitative and quantitative results across diverse indoor/outdoor scenes
Decoupling strategy that separates low-resolution viewpoint tokens from high-resolution image features is intuitive and produces more efficient scene representations
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: individual technical components (cross-attention, Plücker ray representation, Gaussian Splatting) are standard; primary contribution is their integration, which is somewhat incremental

Camera pose dependency underexplored: method requires accurate poses and normalized coordinates; robustness testing (Table 14) only evaluates small perturbations, practical challenges in uncalibrated scenarios remain unclear
Resolution scaling limitations: maximum evaluation at 540×960 resolution; scalability to truly high-resolution inputs (2K, 4K) is not demonstrated, limiting practical applicability

Insufficient mechanistic explanation for Gaussian efficiency: paper shows fewer Gaussians are needed but lacks analysis of why—unclear whether due to representation expressiveness, optimization trajectories, or architectural properties
Hyperparameter sensitivity analysis lacking: perceptual loss weight λ=0.5 in Eq. 5 is set without ablation; robustness to this choice is unexplored
Training computational cost incompletely characterized: Table 8 provides theoretical FLOPs but lacks practical training time comparisons with baselines under identical hardware configurations

Limited analysis of failure modes: while some challenging cases shown, systematic investigation of failures on specular surfaces, thin structures, and occlusions is absent; Section 5 (Limitations) is brief
Generalization questions unaddressed: applicability to different camera models/intrinsics, sensitivity to calibration quality, and performance with significantly fewer views (2-3) remain unexplored
Token uplifting mechanism (Eq. 2) insufficiently justified: linear uplifting is simple but alternatives (non-linear variants) are not explored despite potential benefits
Core insight is straightforward: iterative refinement, while effective, is a relatively obvious design choice conceptually; limited theoretical understanding of why this particular approach succeeds
